title: EA-WM: Event-Aware Generative World Model with Structured Kinematic-to-Visual Action Fields
abstract: arXiv:2605.06192v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Pretrained video diffusion models provide powerful spatiotemporal generative priors, making them a natural foundation for robotic world models. While recent world-action models jointly optimize future videos and actions, they predominantly treat video generation as an auxiliary representation for policy learning. Consequently, they insufficiently explore the inverse problem: leveraging action signals to guide video synthesis, thereby often failing to preserve precise robot spatial geometry and fine-grained robot-object interaction dynamics in the generated rollouts. To bridge this gap, we present EA-WM, an Event-Aware Generative World Model that effectively closes the loop between kinematic control and visual perception. Rather than injecting joint or end-effector actions as abstract, low-dimensional tokens, EA-WM projects actions and kinematic states directly into the target camera view as Structured Kinematic-to-Visual Action

translated_title: EA-WM：具有结构化运动学-视觉动作场的事件感知生成式世界模型
translated_abstract: 预训练视频扩散模型提供了强大的时空生成先验，使其成为构建机器人世界模型的天然基础。尽管近期的世界-动作模型联合优化未来视频与动作，但它们大多将视频生成视为策略学习的辅助表示。因此，它们对逆问题的探索不足：即利用动作信号来引导视频合成，从而在生成的 rollout 中往往无法保持精确的机器人空间几何以及细粒度的机器人-物体交互动态。为弥合这一差距，我们提出了 EA-WM，一个事件感知的生成式世界模型，它有效地闭合了运动学控制与视觉感知之间的回路。EA-WM 并非将关节或末端执行器动作作为抽象的低维 token 注入，而是将动作和运动学状态直接投影到目标相机视图中，形成结构化的运动学-视觉动作场（Structured Kinematic-to-Visual Action Fields）……
tldr: 提出 EA-WM，一种事件感知生成式世界模型，通过将动作与运动学状态直接投影到目标相机视图形成结构化运动学-视觉动作场，实现动作信号引导视频合成，从而在生成轨迹中保持精确的机器人空间几何与细粒度的机器人-物体交互动态。
en_tdlr: EA-WM is an Event-Aware Generative World Model that closes the loop between kinematic control and visual perception by projecting actions and kinematic states directly into the target camera view as Structured Kinematic-to-Visual Action Fields, enabling action signals to guide video synthesis while preserving precise robot spatial geometry and fine-grained robot-object interaction dynamics in generated rollouts.
